extracted.intended_audience: policy analysts, administrative law researchers, agency managers, and statisticians interested in hearing-examiner caseloads
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and interpreting tabular metrics about proceedings handled by agency hearing examiners (counts, ages, dispositions, and time-to-decision) across many federal agencies for fiscal years 1957–1959.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending before examiners at the beginning of the year
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of proceedings pending before hearing examiners at the beginning of the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by agency and year (1957, 1958, 1959). Footnote: 1957 and 1958 figures indicate cases assigned to individual examiners; 1959 figures report all cases referred to the office/chief examiner irrespective of assignment (difference probably slight). NLRB cases may be exceptions due to assignment practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: New cases assigned to examiners during the fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of new cases assigned to hearing examiners during the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported separately by agency and year. Counting conventions note differences between earlier years and 1959 (see footnotes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Old cases remanded or reassigned during the fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of previously existing cases remanded to or reassigned to hearing examiners during the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by agency and year; included as a column in the 'Number of proceedings pending before hearing examiners' table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number disposed of by examiners during the fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of proceedings disposed of (i.e., closed) by hearing examiners during the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by agency and year; these disposals are later broken out by manner of disposition in Table 10 (examiner decision, certification, default/consent/settlement, other).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending before examiners at the end of the year
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of proceedings pending before hearing examiners at the end of the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by agency and year. Footnote explains 1957/1958 vs 1959 counting conventions and exceptions (e.g., Social Security and Indian probate data unavailability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of proceedings reported by the agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxonomy/list of proceeding types (agency-specific categories) for which the tables report counts (e.g., Broadcast licensing; Common carrier services; Safety & special services; Social Security appeals; Indian probate; Cease & desist orders; Certificates of convenience and necessity; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each proceeding type is given with statutory citations (e.g., Broadcast licensing, 47 USC 309,312,316,325,405). The taxonomy drives row labels in the tables and is the basis for per-category statistics; many examples and statutes are listed throughout the tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total pending before examiners at end of year (age table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of cases pending before examiners at the end of the year (used as the base for age-distribution columns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as the first column in the age-of-cases table (Table 9); note data gaps for Social Security and Indian probate in some years (footnotes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending before examiners 3 months or less
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of pending cases at end of year that have been pending 3 months or less before the office of hearing examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age bucket in Table 9; used to evaluate short-term backlog and processing speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending over 3 months but not over 6
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of pending cases at end of year that have been pending more than 3 months but not over 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age bucket in Table 9. Footnote: in one instance (certificate cases) an 865 total reported for 6 months or less is not broken into 0–3 and 3–6; all were placed in 3–6 column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending over 6 months but not over 12
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of pending cases at end of year that have been pending more than 6 months but not over 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age bucket in Table 9; helps identify medium-term backlog.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending more than 1 year
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of pending cases at end of year that have been pending more than one year before the office of hearing examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age bucket in Table 9; footnotes discuss specific suspensions, remands, and cases suspended pending related criminal dispositions affecting long pendency counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total cases disposed of by examiners during the fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate number of cases disposed of by examiners during the fiscal year (Table 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the base for breakdown by manner of disposition (examiner decision after hearing, certified to agency, default/consent/settlement, other examiner disposition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's decision on the merits after evidentiary hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases disposed by examiners via a decision on the merits after an evidentiary (oral) hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 10 column; indicates cases fully decided by examiners following hearings. Footnotes note some dispositions were decided on written submissions without oral hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified to agency upon waiver of examiner's decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases certified to the agency when parties/parties' waiver lead to certification rather than an examiner's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 10 column; denotes matters returned to agency without examiner merits decision because the examiner's decision is waived and the case is certified up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default, consent, settlement, or other agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases disposed by default, consent, settlement, acquiescence, presumed agreement, or similar agreement among parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 10 column; footnote explains 'agreement' includes acquiescence and presumed agreement as well as settlement or other actual agreement. 1957–58 figures in this column may include some procedural dismissals; small misplacements noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other examiner disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases disposed of by the examiner via other dispositions (e.g., dismissed as moot, dismissed for procedural deficiency, decided on written submissions, investigatory hearing cancellations, dispositions following such hearings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 10 last column; footnotes give examples (dismissed as moot or for procedural deficiency; decided on written submissions; investigatory hearing cancelled; suspensions pending related matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total time from assignment to office of hearing examiners to examiner's decision on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall time interval measured from when a case is assigned to the office of hearing examiners until the examiner issues a decision on the merits (Table 11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overall metric is decomposed into discrete time-to-decision buckets (3 months or less; >3–6; >6–12; >1–2 years; over 2 years). It measures end-to-end processing time for decisions on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision rendered in 3 months or less (time-to-decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of examiner decisions on the merits rendered within 3 months or less from assignment to the office of hearing examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 11 time bucket; used as a speed/efficiency indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision rendered over 3 months but not over 6 (time-to-decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of examiner decisions on the merits rendered in over 3 months but not over 6 months from assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 11 time bucket for intermediate processing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision rendered over 6 months but not over 12 (time-to-decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of examiner decisions on the merits rendered in over 6 months but not over 12 months from assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 11 time bucket for longer processing times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision rendered over 1 year but not over 2 (time-to-decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of examiner decisions on the merits rendered in over 1 year but not over 2 years from assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 11 time bucket indicating protracted cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision rendered over 2 years (time-to-decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of examiner decisions on the merits rendered over 2 years from assignment to the office of hearing examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 11 longest time bucket; signals extreme delay. Footnotes mention special circumstances (suspensions, remands, related criminal cases) that can lengthen pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote counting conventions and data gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of counting differences between years and data availability issues (e.g., 1957/1958 numbers reflect cases assigned to individual examiners, 1959 reports all referrals; Social Security and Indian probate data not available in some tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes specify exceptions (e.g., NLRB assignment delays), data unavailability for Social Security/Indian probate causing differences between totals in tables, and special-case suspensions or remands affecting age counts.
